summary: The subject held frozen at the dispatched digest, read-only at both ends, and the prompt held too. This is the hardest row in the family because of the DR-005 rider, and the entry handles it completely: RB-DR005-V2-A1 is carried as operative disposition text with its content quoted and attributed to D-039, clause 1 records 'v2 plus rider', and a dedicated classification block states that Codex's ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES advisory is OPERATIVE rather than leaving it unclassified — which is exactly what D-057 clause 3 requires and what no other row in this family needed. Every pin verifies: six digests, four commits, the Route A remainder an exact four-item match against the disposition's own field, and the register standing of six decisions. The D-028 pin, which the dispatch invites as an attack, is not merely correct but precisely worded.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: c44512ac937c1000a05d813d2b5da148405524bc863bc2d3b95f367beea2d32a, three measurements at start and again at end, equal to the dispatched frozen digest, permissions -r--r--r-- at both ends. The prompt likewise held at d4d3f384b4082a5642e6e8a1258d387e174694914f4a9382bdd4e22e4406cdf5.

The attack 'records v2 without RB-DR005-V2-A1' fails four ways, and this is the row where it could actually have happened. The measured-inputs table records the Codex verdict as 'ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES 0 blockers'. A dedicated pin states 'Operative rider (D-039 / D-057): RB-DR005-V2-A1 is operative disposition text. If the Operational metadata class is denied, doctor fails closed (D-032 BLK-6). This disposition supplies no grant or class admission. Owners record v2 plus this rider.' A separate classification block states 'Codex advisory RB-DR005-V2-A1 is OPERATIVE (carried as the D-039 rider). Claude 2 returned ACCEPT 0/0; no further advisories.' And clause 1 records the disposition '**plus** rider RB-DR005-V2-A1'.

The rider text is faithful to its source. Adopted D-039 records it as 'if the Operational metadata class is denied, doctor fails closed (D-032 BLK-6); this disposition supplies no grant or class admission', and the entry reproduces both limbs.

The classification discharges D-057 clause 3's requirement that an ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES case 'must classify each advisory as non-operative or carry it into the owner record'. It classifies the one advisory as operative and carries it, and states positively that the other reviewer returned no further advisories.

The attack 'D-028 commit pin is false' fails, and the entry is more careful here than it needed to be. It reads 'Route B selection D-028, C-D028, first COORD appearance commit d5721222…'. That commit's subject line names D-035, and I nearly filed this same axis as a blocker on an earlier draft by reading the subject rather than the contents. A git log -S search for the '## D-028 —' heading returns d572122 as the commit that introduced it, so the claim is exactly true and the phrase 'first COORD appearance' states precisely what is being asserted rather than implying the commit is titled D-028.

All six cited digests match live bytes: COORD e53567c0…, file 08 6547e6ac…, the D-054 user amendment, the DR-005 v2 disposition, and both v2 verdicts. The COORD pin is the current post-CONTESTED value.
All four cited commits resolve at full hash: 29670ed… D-054, 33597e8… D-057, d572122… the D-028 first appearance, and 7e7a636… 'D-039: record the DR-005 preview Route B disposition'.

The Route A remainder is complete, tested by string equality against the disposition's whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA: four items each, exact match, same order — applied evidence/retention/D9 integration; executable custody; durable-authoritative negative controls for G19; and full V10 / publication-block demonstration, with the parenthetical noting that D-028 and D-030 both say D-028 does not discharge it.

The register standing supports every dependency: D-054, D-057, D-028, D-039 and D-058 are ADOPTED and not CONTESTED; D-059 is CONTESTED and not ADOPTED. The entry states 'D-058 adopted for DR-002. D-059 is CONTESTED and is not this file', which is accurate.

The attack 'bundled with D-058/D-059' fails: the protocol line states 'This file is one owner-recording entry and one cycle', the header states it does not owner-record any other row, and clause 5 states 'Does not owner-record DR-002, DR-003, DR-004, or DR-008.'

The attacks 'silent SATISFIED', 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'file 08 edited' fail: the header refuses all three, clause 3 states 'Does not mark DR-005 SATISFIED. The Route A remainder above stays owed. Conditions 2–5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization', clause 4 refuses to edit file 08, file 08 measures unchanged and git reports zero modified tracked files.

The attack 'D-057 pin list incomplete' fails: the pins section carries the dependency declaration, the D-054 path with sha256 and commit, the D-057 commit, the D-028 Route B commit, the D-039 coordinator-recording commit, the disposition path with sha256, both verdict paths with sha256s, the owner role, the preview scope, the operative rider, and the advisory classification.

Examined and declined: the owner role reads 'Evidence, storage, and operability authorities' where file 08's DR-005 owner cell reads 'Evidence, storage, operability authorities'. The difference is one conjunction; the three named authorities are identical and no ambiguity is introduced.

Reversibility is the correct compound form and does not reach back into its authorities: 'Compound. Overturn: C-D060, plus reconciliation of any later MF-6 note. Does not overturn D-028, D-039, D-054, or D-057.'

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. DR-005 is the row where the rider could have been dropped, and it is carried four separate ways with its text faithful to adopted D-039 and its advisory explicitly classified as operative — the classify-or-carry rule applied rather than recited. The D-028 pin is the axis the dispatch invited me to attack, and it survives precisely because the entry says 'first COORD appearance' rather than claiming the commit is titled D-028; I tested it by searching for the heading's introduction rather than reading the commit subject, which is the mistake I nearly made on an earlier draft. My one note is dispatch hygiene: the subject is locked, the prompt is not, and the concurrent D-064 dispatch shows the lock is available for both.
